title: indigocat: Delta T table interpolation for 1620-1992 is off by one entry
description:
Found 2026-11-19 in ticket 885c8a5b. get_dynamical_diff_table() in indigo_libs/indigocat/indigocat_dynamical_time.c (JD 2312752.5 - 2448622.5, years 1620-1992) appears to interpolate with an index off by one: it gives 58.0 s at 1990.0 where the table has 56.9 s, 51.5 s at 1991.0 where about 57.6 s is expected, and drops from 119 s at 1620 to 110.5 s at 1621. Reproduce against the table and published values (Meeus / USNO), fix the indexing minimally, check continuity at 1620 and 1992 with the neighbouring branches.
Also include two minor follow-ups from the 885c8a5b review in the same file and test: the comment above get_dynamical_diff_sh2 still says '948 A.D. and 1600 A.D.' (now 1620), and the assertion 'no jump at 1600' in delta_t_matches_observed_values_and_stays_bounded (indigo_test/unit/test_indigocat_corrections.c) compares two points of the same branch; replace it with real continuity checks at the branch boundaries (1620, 1992, 2000). Requires indigo_libs approval (owner approved registering it).

outcome.summary: Pass. indigocat_dynamical_time.c:116-133 now applies Meeus 3.3 correctly: central y2 = delta_t[i], a = y2 - y1, b = y3 - y2, c = b - a, TD = y2 + n/2 (a + b + n c), with n measured in 2-year units from the epoch of delta_t[i] (JD 2312752.5 + 730.5 i, the same epoch formula used to compute i). TERMS 187 matches the initialisers (37 rows of 5 + 2, lines 47-84; the last entry 58.3 is 1992). Bounds: the table branch covers JD [2312752.5, 2448622.5), so i is 0..185; i=0 is clamped to 1, which gives n in [-1,0), still interpolation (n=-1 returns delta_t[0] exactly). The upper clamp TERMS-2=185 is never reached, and delta_t[i+1] stays at most index 186, so nothing reads outside the array. Scratch program linked against the worktree's build/lib/libindigocat.a: every table epoch k=0..185 is reproduced exactly; all 186 mid-interval values lie between their neighbours; the largest step between half-day samples inside the table is 0.006 s. 1992 boundary: 58.294 -> 58.318 (0.024 s, under the test's 0.05 s tolerance). 2000: 63.830/63.830. 1620: 119.021 (sh2, 22.5 t^2 with t = -2.3) -> 124.0 (table entry 0). That 5 s step comes from the difference between the two published sources, and the ticket rightly leaves it out of scope. Minor pre-existing note, not a defect: the 730.5-day epochs drift 3 days behind Gregorian 1 January by 1992 (1700, 1800 and 1900 are not leap years), which causes the 0.024 s residual at 1992. Tests check the exact table values at 8 indices, which I verified against the array (index 40=9.0, 90=13.7, 140=-2.7, 165=29.1, 184=55.8, 185=56.9), plus the mid-values 1621, 1991 (USNO 57.57) and 1951. They also replace the ineffective 1600 assertion with real continuity checks at 1620, 1992 and 2000. The comments are corrected (lines 32, 35, 98, 109). The recorded checks (whitespace, unit) ran on HEAD 74a452ce6, the reviewed tree. Formatting matches the surrounding code.

history.text: Building indigo_libs in worktree to reproduce Delta T table values

Reproduction (scratch tool printing indigocat_get_dynamical_time_diff at JD 2312752.5 + (year-1620)*365.25; table entry from the source / USNO): year before -> after (table | published): 1620 115.000 -> 124.000 (124); 1621 110.500 -> 119.500 (between 124 and 115); 1622 106.000 -> 115.000 (115); 1700 9.000 -> 9.000 (9.0); 1800 13.100 -> 13.700 (13.7); 1900 0.000 -> -2.700 (-2.7 | USNO -2.72); 1950 30.000 -> 29.100 (29.1 | 29.15); 1989 57.487 -> 56.325; 1990 58.300 -> 56.900 (56.9 | 56.86); 1991 51.537 -> 57.562 (between 56.9 and 58.3 | 57.57). Boundaries (value 1e-6 day before / at): 1620 JD 2312752.5 before 119.021/115.000, after 119.021/124.000; 1992 JD 2448622.5 before 59.572/58.318, after 58.294/58.318; 2000 JD 2451544.5 63.830/63.830 unchanged.
Root cause: get_dynamical_diff_table() measured n from the epoch of delta_t[i] but used delta_t[i+1] as the central value of Meeus formula 3.3, so every value was shifted one table entry (two years) late; c was also computed as a - b instead of b - a; and for 1990..1992 the third point delta_t[i+2] was the zero filler after the last real entry (TERMS 192 with 187 initialisers), which produced the 51.5 s at 1991.
Fix: central entry delta_t[i] with neighbours i-1 and i+1, i clamped to 1..TERMS-2, c = b - a, TD = delta_t[i] + n/2 (a + b + n c); TERMS 192 -> 187 (the real entry count, so no zero filler can be read). Comments 1600 -> 1620 above get_dynamical_diff_sh2 and the table function.
